Examples are the `hs0`/`hρs0` nonzero-from-valuation-one pattern, the two inertia residue-field unfoldings, and the two `A.valuation (algebraMap ... (z * n))` computations. I did not look at the Lean-side details of `Algebra.IsInvariant.exists_smul_of_under_eq_of_profinite`, so the sketched rewrite is untested. The `Gal(ℂ̄/L)` action on `integralClosure ℤ ℂ̄` in the first proof is a local `letI` built with `MulSemiringAction.compHom` from `rsh`. The shared lemma is therefore stated as a fixed-point-set openness lemma (`g b = b`) and a rational-descent lemma, not as an instance. The `ContinuousSMul` and `IsInvariant` instance wrappers stay local to each proof.

findings.problem: Two long proofs contain the same two-part argument, once over `L` (lines 614–646) and once over `ℚ` (lines 1007–1042). (1) For integral `b`, the stabiliser of `b` in `Gal(ℂ̄/K)` is open. It contains `fixingSubgroup (adjoin K {b})`, the adjoin is finite-dimensional by integrality, and `Subgroup.isOpen_mono` finishes. (2) For `b` in `integralClosure ℤ ℂ̄` fixed by all `g`, `b = algebraMap K ℂ̄ y` for some `y` that is integral over ℤ. This uses `InfiniteGalois.mem_range_algebraMap_iff_fixed`, then the `hyint` polynomial transfer using `Polynomial.hom_eval₂`, `map_zero` and the `convert ... using 2 <;> first | rfl | exact Subsingleton.elim _ _` step. The only differences are `K = L` versus `K = ℚ` and the last step. Any change to the argument, such as a Mathlib API rename, has to be made in two places inside already very large proofs. The `L` proof is also slow enough to need `maxHeartbeats 8000000`.
findings.proposed_change:
Add two general lemmas over `K : IntermediateField ℚ (AlgebraicClosure ℚ)`, or over any field `K` with `Algebra K (AlgebraicClosure ℚ)`. Gal(ℂ̄/K) stands for `AlgebraicClosure ℚ ≃ₐ[K] AlgebraicClosure ℚ`, and `(b : ℂ̄)` ranges over elements of `integralClosure ℤ ℂ̄`.
(a) `isOpen_fixing_of_isIntegral (K) (b : ℂ̄) (hb : IsIntegral ℤ b) : IsOpen {g : Gal(ℂ̄/K) | g b = b}`. Proof: the existing body, namely `adjoin.finiteDimensional`, `fixingSubgroup_isOpen`, `isOpen_mono` and `mem_fixingSubgroup_iff`.
(b) `exists_integral_preimage_of_fixed (K) (b : integralClosure ℤ ℂ̄) (hb : ∀ g : Gal(ℂ̄/K), g • b = b) : ∃ y : K, algebraMap K ℂ̄ y = b ∧ IsIntegral ℤ y`. Proof: lines 633–643 verbatim.
Then, at line 616, the `ContinuousSMul` becomes `continuousSMul_iff_stabilizer_isOpen.mpr fun b => by simpa [MulAction.stabilizer] using isOpen_fixing_of_isIntegral L b b.2`. The `IsInvariant` instance at line 631 becomes `obtain ⟨y, hy, hyint⟩ := exists_integral_preimage_of_fixed L b hb` followed by `⟨⟨y, hyint⟩, Subtype.ext hy⟩`. Lines 1009 and 1024 reduce to the same calls with `K = ℚ`, plus the existing `IsIntegrallyClosed` step for `ℤ`. The `L` case may need `change` to match the local `actL` action; it is definitionally `g b`.
findings.benefit: Each of the two big proofs loses about 30 lines of topological and descent boilerplate. The lemmas state plainly what is used, namely openness of fixed sets of integral elements and descent of Galois-fixed integral elements to `K`. A future fix then needs to be made in one place.
